verdict.rationale: Grok Bot is itself a built-in AI assistant. Users hand off jobs by message: "describe the job, and grant access as it asks." The Bot then works on its own persistent cloud computer while the laptop is closed, and Bots can pass ownership of tasks to each other. Month-long hands-on users confirm that async delegation "actually works," including a bot that negotiated with about 40 suppliers on its own.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: Setup is a message, not a workflow builder. Create a Bot, describe the job, and grant access as it asks.
Your Bots run on a persistent cloud computer with a browser, filesystem, and terminal... and work continues while your laptop is closed.
anything you hand off to a Bot won't count against your existing usage.
pass ownership of a task, so you aren't the router between tools.
Because each bot has its own computer, async work 'actually works.'
one bot contacted ~40 fabric suppliers in Vietnam, negotiated prices, locked one in and got samples made for custom swag.
